text:
anna: Heads-up — nightly SAST flagged a recurring pattern across ui/* that looks like `new Function(...)` / dynamic eval usage in ~130 files. Not all callsites are exploitable but it's widespread. https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/12801 :eyes:

dave: Can you paste a sample file/stack? Is this a third-party lib or our code?

anna: It's in our code, mostly tiny helpers under ui/utils. Example: 
```js
// ui/utils/parser.js
export function compileTemplate(t) {
  return new Function('data', `with(data){return ${t}}`);
}
```
Found with: `rg "new Function\(|eval\(" ui/ -n`

sast-bot: SAST run complete — 130 findings (low=92, med=34, high=4). Top folders: ui/ (62), shared/ (30), examples/ (38). Rule: DYN-EVAL-01. Link: https://sast.internal/reports/4389991112

priya: I own most of ui/*. I'll triage but low-level evals are used for the email/template renderer. We intentionally allow simple string templates.

anna: Understood. My concern: some callsites feed network-controlled data into templates. We should add a taint check before rule suppression. Right now CI flags everything, causing noise.

tom: Are scanners using ephemeral creds that show who ran them? We should ensure audit logs link SAST runs to service accounts. Also we can grant the scanner ephemeral KMS decrypt if needed for artifact fetch — but that needs an RBAC change request.

priya: There's one failing premerge job because of the blanket rule. If we suppress, we need a test case proving no user-controlled input reaches `compileTemplate`.

anna: Proposed plan: 1) create a lightweight evidence harness per module (unit tests that exercise template paths with simulated user input), 2) add a CI-only `sast:evidence` label to PRs that attach those tests, 3) update SAST config to only escalate to med/high when taint analysis indicates network input.

dave: Sounds reasonable. We should avoid adding a global suppression. Also want to avoid blocking deploys for low noise. Can we make the gating behavior: block only if >5 high/critical or if a new high appears in prod code paths?

anna: Yes. I'll open a follow-up RFC for the gating thresholds, but immediate action is triage for this pattern.

priya: I'll start by adding tests for the email renderer and attach to the PR. Quick question — where do we put the `sast:evidence` tests? Under `ui/__tests__/sast-evidence/`?

anna: That works. Name the tests `evidence.sast.js` and include the exact input string that used to trigger the rule. Also add a small README explaining why suppression is safe.

oncall-security: Please add a link to the audit log for the SAST run when you open the PR so we can correlate. Also add `#sec-review` to the PR checklist.

tom: About RBAC: granting scanner ephemeral KMS decrypt to pull closed artifacts requires a one-time policy change. I can prepare a request template. We should scope it to the `sast-runner@infra` service account and a single key: `artifact-encryption-prod`.

priya: For the immediate CI unblock I'm going to add a conditional suppression in `.sast/config.yml` for `ui/templates/*` but gated by the presence of `sast:evidence` label. Example snippet: 
```yaml
rules:
  DYN-EVAL-01:
    suppress_when_label: sast:evidence
    require_evidence_path: ui/__tests__/sast-evidence/evidence.sast.js
```

anna: Works for me as long as the CI enforcer verifies the `require_evidence_path`. I'll add a small check in the SAST GH action to fail if suppression is used without the evidence file present.

dave: Add me as reviewer on the infra RBAC change and the CI check PR.

priya: creating PR now, will ping when ready.

sast-bot: New suppression attempted in branch `priya/ui-template-fix`. Verification pending: evidence file not yet present.

priya: Added evidence test + README. Link: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/12801/files

anna: Verified evidence locally. Running targeted DAST on the example endpoints to ensure runtime behavior hasn't regressed.

oncall-security: Great. Once the DAST run completes, attach the HTML report here. If anything suspicious shows up, escalate to incident response.

priya: DAST finished — no exploitable template injection found in logged endpoints. Attaching report: https://dast-reports.internal/4389991112-report.html

dave: Ok, move forward with the conditional suppression and CI enforcer. Tom, please open the RBAC change request; link it to the PR for traceability.

tom: Will do. Drafting now and routing to security-approvers@redwood. Expect request ID RBAC-2026-112.

anna: I'll update the SAST runbook with the new `sast:evidence` flow and add a small playbook entry on how to handle widespread low-severity patterns.

priya: Thank you all. Closing the immediate noise. Will follow up if any findings crop up in canary. :thumbsup:

oncall-security: Closing thread unless any objections. If anyone wants to reopen, ping me. :lock:
